thread:
Maya Chen: quick Q about the RPC async endpoint contract — are we standardizing on a single `request_id` + polling response shape for both hosted and dedicated? trying to finalize an example for the client SDK docs.

Tim O'Leary: @Maya yeah we should. Are you thinking the server returns an immediate 202 with a `location` header + body, or 200 with a payload that includes the poll URL? we have existing callers expecting both.

Maya Chen: pref would be 202 + `Location` header for new endpoints, but we need backcompat guidance. if older callers get 200 we should document both patterns and normalize in the SDK.

Sarah Park: proposal: server returns `202 Accepted` and body with { "request_id": "..", "poll_url": "/v1/jobs/{id}", "eta_seconds": 12 } to make it explicit. poll endpoint returns status objects. quick schema:

```json
{
  "status": "queued|running|completed|failed|cancelled",
  "request_id": "string",
  "result_url": "string?",
  "error": "string?",
  "progress": "number?",
  "updated_at": "2024-10-01T12:34:56Z"
}
```

Sarah Park: also suggest `Retry-After` on 202 to hint clients about backoff, and include `idempotency_key` echo if provided.

Ryan Patel: two edgecases: 1) client cancels a request mid-processing — do we mark job as `cancelled` immediately or wait until the worker notices? 2) what does the cancel API return if job already finished?

Maya Chen: for 1) we should accept the cancel request and return 202 with `cancellation_in_progress` (or just 202 + no body) and update status to `cancelled` only when worker confirms. doc should call out eventual consistency.

Tim O'Leary: for 2) cancel on finished job -> return 409 with body { "error": "job_already_completed", "request_id": "..." } ? alternatively 204 No Content to be idempotent. leaning to 409 so clients can surface a clear message.

Sarah Park: prefer idempotent safe response. 204 if already completed or already cancelled (so retries are no-ops). 409 for conflict when caller expects to cancel and we want to force them to handle manually. happy to pick one but document clearly.

Ryan Patel: SDK-wise we can map both 204 and 409 into typed errors. also need to agree on canonical field name: `request_id` vs `job_id` — pick `request_id` for consistency with other RPCs.

Maya Chen: agreed. one more: backwards compatibility — if older endpoints return `200` with an embedded `status: queued`, we should still parse into the new shape in SDK. I'll add a transform.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for service=jobs-api tag=canary-2024.10.3. Expected window 10m :rocket:

Tim O'Leary: thanks — can we add a small regression test: simulate client cancel -> worker acknowledges -> poll shows `cancelled` within 30s? if not, fail.

Sarah Park: I'll add tests and update the API spec PR with the JSON examples and the cancel edgecase table.

Maya Chen: perfect. I'll update the SDK doc draft with the 202 + Location example and backcompat note. ping me in the PR @Sarah @Tim if you see anything off. :thumbsup:

Ryan Patel: lgtm, will review tests once PR is up.

Maya Chen: thanks all.
